q: Make the case for the Côte des Bar: where it is, what it is planted to, and why its geology sets it apart from the Marne.
accept: the aube on kimmeridgian marl planted mostly to pinot noir near chablis
southern champagne closer to chablis with kimmeridgian clay and limestone soils
aube vineyard about a quarter of plantings dominated by pinot noir
kimmeridgian marl rather than marne chalk warmer and pinot noir country
ans: The Côte des Bar is the Aube's vineyard, around 120 km southeast of Épernay — nearer to Chablis than to Reims, and warmer. It carries roughly a quarter of Champagne's plantings, on the order of 8,000 hectares of about 34,000, and it is overwhelmingly Pinot Noir, well over 80% of the area. Crucially its soil is Kimmeridgian marl of Upper Jurassic age, the same limestone-and-clay band that runs through Chablis and on toward Sancerre, not the Cretaceous belemnite and micraster chalk of the Marne. That means more clay, more water retention, more warmth and riper, rounder Pinot. Historically it was the volume supplier the Marne looked down on and tried to legislate out of the region — the 1911 riots were exactly that fight — and it long fed the big houses' blends anonymously. Today Cédric Bouchard, Vouette et Sorbée, Drappier and Fleury have made it a source of named-site Champagne in its own right, and it also holds the still Rosé des Riceys.
exp: Geology explains the flavour: the Aube's clay-rich Kimmeridgian and southern latitude give fruit weight and generosity, where the Marne's pure chalk gives the tension and salinity of the Côte des Blancs. It also explains the politics — an appellation boundary drawn through two different geological systems was always going to be contested, and the region's finest growers now argue the Aube was never the lesser half, only the cheaper one.
May 15, 1936 — the INAO's first decree wave.

q: The EU's PDO 'evocation' doctrine punished which famous cases?
accept: glen buchenbach champagner sorbet parmesan style
ans: e.g., 'Glen Buchenbach' German whisky (CJEU C-44/17, 2018) and Queso Manchego's figurative signs (C-614/17, 2019) — evocation can infringe without copying the protected name; 'Champagner Sorbet' (C-393/16, 2017) went the other way, and turned on use of the PDO's reputation rather than evocation
exp: IP law is now oral material; know one case name.

ans: 'Japan Wine' = 100% domestically grown grapes; GIs like Yamanashi and Hokkaido formalized
exp: Koshu's international push required legal hygiene first.

q: Switzerland's Grand Cru logic and its most famous white appellation:
ans: Cantonal Grand Cru rules; Dézaley (Lavaux terraces) — Chasselas' greatest stage
exp: UNESCO terraces above Lac Léman; the orals' favorite 'invisible' country.

q: 'Vino de Pueblo' and 'Vi de Vila' represent:
accept: village wine movements spain priorat rioja
ans: Spain's village-wine tiers (Priorat's Vi de Vila first, Rioja's municipio after) — Burgundy grammar in Spanish
exp: The Iberian classification convergence is a running oral theme.

q: What must a US label's 'Contains Sulfites' threshold be, and the allergen-labeling twist in the EU?
accept: 10 ppm eu adds egg milk fining disclosure
10 mg/l sulfites eu allergens casein albumin
ans: ≥10 ppm triggers the sulfite statement (both); the EU also requires egg/milk fining-agent disclosure
exp: Hence 'vegan' labeling's rise — the fining agents outed themselves.

q: The 2023 EU rules added what to wine labels?
ans: Ingredient and nutrition disclosure (on-label energy, QR e-labels for the rest)
exp: December 2023 — ask any importer about the scramble.

q: Explain how an appellation's rules can be changed, using one real example.
accept: consorzio or syndicat proposes inao approves chianti gran selezione uga
ans: The producers' body petitions the national authority (INAO, consorzio → Ministry, TTB): e.g., Chianti Classico's UGA additions in 2023, or Bordeaux's 2021 climate varieties
exp: Appellations are living documents written by whoever shows up to vote.

q: Explain why 'organic' and 'biodynamic' certifications say nothing about wine quality.
accept: farming practice certifications not quality standards
ans: They certify permitted inputs and farming practice, not the resulting wine's quality — a badly made organic wine is still badly made
exp: Correlation exists because attentive farmers tend to certify; causation does not.

q: Explain how a producer can lose the right to use an appellation.
accept: failing the agrément tasting panel rejection loss of aoc status
ans: Wines must pass the agrément — an analytical and tasting approval. Failure means declassification; persistent failure or rule breach can cost a producer the right to the name
exp: Which is how a grower ends up in Vin de France by force rather than choice.

q: Explain why some great producers deliberately declassify.
accept: rules forbid their blend or style freedom from panel
ans: Because the rules forbid their grape, blend or style, or because the tasting panel rejects atypical wine — Deiss, Anselmi, Gravner, Artadi, Luís Pato all chose the lower tier
exp: A low appellation on a great label is usually a statement.

q: Explain what 'Grand Cru' guarantees, and does not, in Burgundy.
accept: site not producer no quality guarantee land only
ans: It classifies the land, not the grower — it guarantees provenance and yield rules, never the quality of the bottle in front of you
exp: There is bad grand cru; say so plainly when asked.

q: Explain the labeling requirements for a wine sold in the United States.
accept: brand class type alcohol net contents name address sulfite government warning
ans: Brand name, class/type, alcohol, net contents, bottler's name and address, sulfite declaration and the Government Warning — all on a TTB-approved COLA
exp: Import compliance is part of a beverage director's job.

q: What is the VDP, how does its classification work, and what is its relationship to German wine law?
accept: a private growers association with gutswein ortswein erste lage and grosse lage
voluntary and stricter than the law with grosses gewachs as the dry summit
private classification whose logic the 2021 reform adopted
not law at all but a trademarked members club with its own site rankings
ans: The Verband Deutscher Prädikatsweingüter is a private association of around two hundred growers, not a legal authority; its eagle capsule is a trademark, and membership is contractual and can be lost. Its pyramid runs Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage and Grosse Lage, with a dry wine from a Grosse Lage labelled Grosses Gewächs. Members accept yield caps, hand harvesting, later picking and a permitted-variety list for each classified site, all stricter than the law requires, and they have largely reserved the Prädikat terms for wines with sweetness. Its significance is that German statutory law was reformed from 2021 onto the same territorial logic — the narrower the origin, the higher the claim — so the state moved toward the VDP rather than the other way round, and terms the association invented are being drawn into the law itself.
exp: Say the words 'not law' early. Any member could resign tomorrow and lose nothing legal, which is precisely why the VDP polices its own sites so publicly. It is the clearest modern case of a private body classifying land faster and more credibly than a state could.

q: Explain Barolo's Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive — what they are, and what they emphatically are not.
accept: 181 mapped names since 2010 that delimit vineyards but establish no hierarchy
additional geographical mentions which delimit crus without ranking them
mga names are legally equal and were drawn by negotiation
they map barolo but there is no grand cru tier in the rules
ans: Introduced in 2010, the additional geographical mentions map the Barolo zone into 181 named units — vineyard areas plus commune-wide mentions that let a producer say, for example, Barolo del Comune di La Morra. A wine carrying an MGA must come entirely from within it, and the word Vigna may be added only with a narrower named plot inside the MGA and under stricter conditions. What they do not do is rank. There is no grand cru and no premier cru anywhere in the decree; every MGA is legally equal. The boundaries were drawn by negotiation among growers and communes, so several celebrated names were enlarged well beyond their historic core and some MGAs cover ground of very mixed quality. Price and reputation do the ranking that the law declined to do.
exp: Delimiting and ranking are two separate acts, and Piedmont deliberately did only the first — partly because ranking is what turns a consorzio vote into a lawsuit. Have Cannubi's boundary enlargement ready as the concrete example of what negotiation does to a map.
